I could not derive or verify this count from first principles, and I don't have a reliable recollection of the published classification.

The problem asks for the number of equivalence classes of symmetric Hadamard matrices of order 28 under signed-permutation equivalence. Settling this requires either a complete classification or an exhaustive computer search, and I can't do either by hand here. I also have not checked whether the relation $K = PHQ^T$ (with $P$ and $Q$ independent, and $K$ required to be symmetric) gives the same classes as the more common $PHP^T$ equivalence for symmetric matrices.

My best recollection is that the number is 14, but I have low confidence in that value. Please check it against the classification literature on symmetric Hadamard matrices of order 28 before relying on it.

ANSWER: 14
